title: Settling the Fixed Monthly Sum of a Standing Automatic Payment on Personal Credit Cards
content:
### The payable balance

The payable balance is the charges standing on the card ledger, being its purchases, cash advances, cash advance and other fees, billed interest, returned payments and dispute rebills, less the credits standing on it, being its payments, merchant credits, fee reversals, interest reversals, dispute credits and rewards statement credits, and never less than 0.00 USD.

### The coverage share, the spread and the addition

The coverage share is 50 percent, and it acts on the payable balance alone. The amount is spread over 1 statement cycle. No carryover addition is made, the carryover addition standing at 0.00 USD.

### Rounding and ceiling

The figure is rounded half-up to the cent, and the fixed monthly amount is the lesser of that figure and the payable balance. The fixed monthly amount of a standing automatic payment instruction on a card under Personal Credit Cards is worked out by the desk from the payable balance and never exceeds it.

### Worked on hypothetical figures

A card ledger carries purchases of 2400.00 USD, cash advances of 300.00 USD, fees of 73.00 USD, billed interest of 128.60 USD, a returned payment of 200.00 USD and a dispute rebill of 150.00 USD, against payments of 1100.00 USD, merchant credits of 60.00 USD, fee reversals of 14.35 USD, interest reversals of 0.00 USD, dispute credits of 222.88 USD and rewards statement credits of 55.00 USD. The charges total 3251.60 USD and the credits total 1452.23 USD, so the payable balance is 1799.37 USD.

The coverage share acting on that balance gives 899.685 USD; spread over 1 statement cycle it is unchanged; rounded half-up to the cent it is 899.69 USD; and the lesser of 899.69 USD and 1799.37 USD is 899.69 USD.

Where the credits standing on a card ledger exceed its charges, the difference is below zero and the payable balance is 0.00 USD, so the fixed monthly amount is 0.00 USD as well.
